nuggets.title: Polling the Job Store Saturates Database CPU

scenario.symptoms: Scheduler DB CPU pegs at 95% during peak. Job dispatch latency rises from 200ms to 8s. EXPLAIN shows millions of SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED scans per minute.
scenario.interviewerSetup: 500 worker processes poll the jobs table every 100ms with no indexing on (status, run_at). Table holds 50M historical completed rows.

incident.headline: Hot job store design causes database meltdown under high-frequency worker polling

agenda.goal: Store schedulable jobs in an indexed hot table with archival, or use a queue/log built for dispatch workloads.
agenda.opener: Our Postgres job table melted during peak. How should scheduled tasks be persisted and queried?

evidence.strong: Partial index on pending jobs, partition or archive completed work, lease-based claim, consider Kafka/SQS for dispatch with DB for metadata, backoff polling.
evidence.adequate: Adds index but keeps all history in one table.

misconceptions.pattern: Assumes any relational table works for high-QPS dispatch.
misconceptions.challenge: How many polls/sec hit the DB with 500 workers?

probes: What rows must be in the hot path?
When do you move jobs to cold storage?
agenda.referenceFix: Hot pending table with index on (status, run_at), archive pipeline, adaptive poll interval.

nuggets.title: Clock Skew Causes the Same Job to Run Twice

scenario.symptoms: Billing export job emails customers duplicate PDFs. Two workers claim the same job_id within 500ms during NTP drift on one host.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Leases expire based on worker wall clock without fencing tokens. Slow worker resumes after lease appears expired to another worker.

incident.headline: Weak lease semantics allow duplicate execution after clock skew and slow workers

agenda.goal: Use store-monotonic leases with fencing tokens and idempotent job handlers.
agenda.opener: Two workers ran the same billing export and customers got duplicate emails. How do leases prevent double execution?

evidence.strong: Lease expiry based on store time, monotonic lease generation/fencing token passed to downstream, heartbeats, job handler idempotency keys.
evidence.weak: Optimistic lock without handling slow workers.

misconceptions.pattern: Believes longer TTL alone prevents overlap.
misconceptions.challenge: What if worker A pauses for GC longer than TTL?

probes: Who is the source of truth for time?
How does downstream reject stale workers?
hints: Fencing token increments on each claim.
Jobs should be safe to retry.
agenda.referenceFix: Central lease service with fencing tokens, idempotent side effects, heartbeats.

nuggets.title: Single Leader Scheduler Drops Minute Cron Tasks

scenario.symptoms: During leader failover, 18% of minute-level cron tasks never enqueue. Metrics show a 90-second gap in schedule ticks.
scenario.interviewerSetup: One active scheduler leader fires all cron expressions; standby takes 90s to acquire lock after leader pod OOM.

incident.headline: Single-leader cron tick loop misses schedules during slow failover

agenda.goal: Run highly available scheduling with fast leader election and catch-up of missed fire times.
agenda.opener: We missed a minute of cron fires when the scheduler leader died. How should the scheduler component scale and fail over?

evidence.strong: Fast leader election, missed tick reconciliation on new leader, optional sharded schedulers by job namespace, persistent next_run_at per job.
evidence.adequate: Hot standby with manual failover runbook.

misconceptions.pattern: Confuses scaling workers with scaling the cron tick generator.
misconceptions.challenge: Who enqueues jobs at exactly 09:00 UTC?

probes: Can cron be sharded by tenant?
hints: Leader only ticks clocks; workers execute.
agenda.referenceFix: HA leader with sub-10s failover, backfill missed schedules idempotently.

nuggets.title: DST Transition Fires Hourly Job Twice or Skips Once

scenario.symptoms: Finance reconciliation ran twice on fall-back night and skipped entirely on spring-forward in US/Eastern cron jobs.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Cron expressions interpreted in local timezone without storing UTC next_run or using robust recurrence library.

incident.headline: Naive timezone cron handling duplicates or skips recurring jobs on DST boundaries

agenda.goal: Store next run in UTC with timezone-aware recurrence rules and explicit DST policy.
agenda.opener: Our nightly job ran twice when clocks rolled back. How do you define and fire recurring schedules across timezones?

evidence.strong: Persist next_run_at UTC, use tz database rules, document skip vs run-once policy for ambiguous hours, iCal RRULE or mature library.
evidence.adequate: UTC only cron without customer timezones.

misconceptions.pattern: Stores cron string without timezone context.
misconceptions.challenge: What is 2am America/New_York on DST fall-back day?

probes: Should a missed hour be skipped or run when time jumps?
How do you test DST edges?
agenda.referenceFix: UTC next_run with tz-aware computation, explicit DST policies in job metadata.

nuggets.title: One Tenant's Job Flood Starves Everyone Else

scenario.symptoms: Platform-wide job latency SLO breaches while one enterprise tenant enqueues 2M backup jobs in an hour. Other tenants wait hours in FIFO queue.
scenario.interviewerSetup: Single shared queue with global FIFO ordering and fixed worker pool without fair scheduling or per-tenant caps.

incident.headline: Global FIFO scheduling lets one tenant's hotkey workload monopolize all workers

agenda.goal: Isolate tenants with fair queuing, rate limits, and weighted scheduling across pools.
agenda.opener: One customer enqueue storm blocked every other tenant's jobs. How do you prevent hotkey tenants from starving the platform?

evidence.strong: Per-tenant queues or weighted fair queuing, enqueue rate limits, dedicated pools for large tenants, priority tiers with caps.

misconceptions.pattern: Adds workers assuming they help all tenants equally.
misconceptions.challenge: If FIFO has 2M jobs from tenant A first, who runs tenant B's job?

probes: How do you cap enqueue rate?
When does a tenant get a dedicated queue?
hints: Fairness across tenants, not just throughput.
Rate limit at API layer too.
agenda.referenceFix: Per-tenant queues with WFQ, enqueue quotas, burst isolation.
